smbv1_enabled.title: SMBv1 / CIFS Dialect Enabled
smbv1_enabled.description: Whether the legacy SMBv1/CIFS dialect is enabled on the file server (EnableSMB1Protocol). SMBv1 lacks signing, encryption, and pre-auth integrity and is the protocol exploited by the wormable EternalBlue / MS17-010 remote-code-execution flaw (WannaCry, NotPetya). Secure value: false (SMBv1 disabled/removed).

min_smb_dialect.title: Minimum Negotiable SMB Dialect
min_smb_dialect.description: The minimum SMB dialect the server will negotiate with clients. A floor that still permits SMB1/CIFS leaves the EternalBlue surface reachable via protocol downgrade from hardened SMB3; Microsoft guidance is to force a SMB 3.1.1 minimum (which provides pre-auth integrity that blocks downgrade). Secure value: SMB3.1.1 (or any SMB3.x floor); insecure when the floor is CIFS/SMB1/SMB1.0.

edge_appliance_patched_within_sla.title: Edge Appliance Patched Within SLA
edge_appliance_patched_within_sla.description: Shared-vocabulary attestation: the file-server / NAS appliance OS, firmware, and bundled apps are kept on current, vendor-supported versions and patched within the organisation's remediation SLA, including the MS17-010 SMBv1 RCE fix and CISA-KEV-listed CVEs (e.g. CVE-2021-28799 QNAP HBS 3, CVE-2022-27593 QNAP Photo Station). Secure value is true; the exposure fires when false (lagging firmware leaves the appliance on the brute-force / mass-exploit surface and gives ransomware a foothold). Reused across vectors that depend on edge-appliance patch hygiene.

everyone_full_control_share.title: Share Grants Everyone Full Control
everyone_full_control_share.description: Interpreted boolean: at least one SMB share grants Everyone or Authenticated Users Full Control / Change on data. Modelled as an interpreted boolean rather than a raw ACL string because the security depends on interpreting the principal+right pair. Fires (true) on the over-broad, least-privilege-violating configuration; the hardened baseline scopes named groups to minimum rights (false).

nfs_export_wildcard_rw.title: NFS Export Wildcard Read-Write
nfs_export_wildcard_rw.description: Interpreted boolean: at least one NFS export uses a wildcard client spec ('*' or 0.0.0.0/0) combined with blanket read-write (rw), so any reachable host can read/tamper with/mass-encrypt the export. Modelled as an interpreted boolean because the hazard is the host-scope + access-mode combination. Fires (true) on the over-broad export; the hardened baseline binds exports to explicit trusted subnets (false).

least_privilege_access_enforced.title: Least-Privilege Access Enforced
least_privilege_access_enforced.description: Shared-workspace vocabulary attestation: least-privilege access control is enforced across the file store's shares/exports — principals receive only the minimum rights required (named groups, ro where writes are not needed) and no broad principal holds Full Control. Fires (is_false) when least privilege is NOT enforced, i.e. the store's access model is over-broad. The all-secure baseline sets it true (silent) and the all-insecure baseline false (fires).

access_based_enumeration_disabled.title: Access-Based Enumeration Disabled
access_based_enumeration_disabled.description: Interpreted boolean: Access-Based Enumeration (ABE) is disabled on shares (FolderEnumerationMode = Unrestricted), so all file/folder names are visible to any user regardless of permission, exposing sensitive names for reconnaissance. Named for the insecure state so it fires (is_true) when ABE is off; the hardened baseline enables ABE (false). Secondary exposure facet amplifying the over-broad-share weakness.

insecure_guest_auth_allowed.title: Insecure Guest Authentication Allowed
insecure_guest_auth_allowed.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the SMB client/server permits insecure guest logons (AllowInsecureGuestAuth=1 / EnableSecurityGuest). Guest logons require no password and disable SMB signing/encryption, permitting unauthenticated share enumeration and access. Secure value is false (AllowInsecureGuestAuth=0), so this exposure fires only on the insecure (true) config.

null_session_access_allowed.title: Anonymous Null-Session Access Allowed
null_session_access_allowed.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the SMB server permits anonymous null-session connections (RestrictNullSessAccess=0, RestrictAnonymous low, or named pipes/shares reachable without credentials), allowing unauthenticated enumeration of shares, users, and the host. Secure value is false (null sessions restricted), so this exposure fires only when null-session access is open (true).

nfs_auth_sys_only.title: NFS Relies on AUTH_SYS Only
nfs_auth_sys_only.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when NFS exports carrying accessible data rely solely on AUTH_SYS (sec=sys / no sec= option) with no RPCSEC_GSS Kerberos flavor (krb5/krb5i/krb5p). AUTH_SYS trusts client-supplied UIDs with no cryptographic authentication, so any reachable client can mount and access exports by spoofing UIDs — effectively unauthenticated access. Secure value is false (krb5i/krb5p enforced on sensitive exports), so this exposure fires only on the insecure (sec=sys-only) config.

smb_signing_required.title: SMB Signing Required
smb_signing_required.description: Whether the SMB server mandates SMB message signing (RequireSecuritySignature). Secure value is true (signing required). When false, signing is optional and an adjacent attacker can perform an SMB relay / signing-downgrade attack to tamper with sessions and steal credentials.

smb3_encryption_required.title: SMB3 Encryption Required
smb3_encryption_required.description: Whether SMB3 end-to-end encryption (AES-128/256-GCM/CCM) is required for SMB traffic server-wide or per share (EncryptData). Secure value is true. When false, cleartext SMB transport is permitted and an adjacent attacker can sniff/MITM SMB traffic to steal credentials and data in transit.

reject_unencrypted_access.title: Reject Unencrypted Access
reject_unencrypted_access.description: When SMB encryption is enabled, whether the server rejects clients that cannot negotiate SMB3 encryption (RejectUnencryptedAccess, default true). Secure value is true. When false, non-SMB3 / SMB1/SMB2 clients are allowed onto encrypted shares, re-opening a cleartext downgrade path the AiTM attacker can force.

smb_ntlm_blocked.title: NTLM Blocked for SMB
smb_ntlm_blocked.description: Whether NTLM authentication is blocked for SMB so Kerberos is enforced (BlockNTLM). Secure value is true (NTLM blocked, Kerberos-only). When false, NTLM is permitted and a negotiated downgrade from Kerberos to NTLM enables NTLM relay, pass-the-hash, and challenge-response leakage to a malicious/spoofed server.

nfs_export_security_flavor.title: NFS Export Security Flavor
nfs_export_security_flavor.description: The RPCSEC_GSS authentication/integrity/privacy flavor for NFS exports (sec= in /etc/exports). Secure values are krb5i (integrity) or krb5p (Kerberos auth + integrity + on-the-wire encryption). The insecure value 'sys' (AUTH_SYS, the default when no sec= is set) trusts client-supplied UIDs with no cryptographic authentication and carries traffic in cleartext, allowing UID spoofing and sniffing/MITM of AUTH_SYS NFS traffic.

nfs_no_root_squash_set.title: NFS no_root_squash Set
nfs_no_root_squash_set.description: Interpreted from the NFS export options: true when any export carries the no_root_squash option, which trusts the client's root (UID 0) and lets a client-root attacker read/write server-side files as root (drop SUID binaries, alter ACLs, tamper with data) — a privilege-escalation/data-tampering exposure. The secure default is root_squash (client root mapped to anonymous nfsnobody), under which this is false.

immutable_worm_snapshots_enabled.title: Immutable WORM Snapshots Enabled
immutable_worm_snapshots_enabled.description: Whether the store keeps immutable/WORM (read-only, retention-locked) point-in-time snapshots that ransomware cannot delete or encrypt. Insecure (false) when there are no snapshots, or snapshots are deletable/writable by an account ransomware can compromise — the core enabler of irrecoverable mass-encryption (Qlocker/DeadBolt/eCh0raix).

offline_airgapped_backup_exists.title: Offline / Air-Gapped Backup Exists
offline_airgapped_backup_exists.description: Whether at least one backup copy is offline/air-gapped/immutable (3-2-1-1 style), unreachable from the production credentials/network. Insecure (false) when the only backups are online and reachable from the same credentials/network as production storage, so ransomware that reaches the store can also destroy the last-resort copy.

ransomware_mass_change_detection_enabled.title: Ransomware Mass-Change Detection Enabled
ransomware_mass_change_detection_enabled.description: Whether bulk-modify/rename/encrypt anomaly detection is in place to surface ransomware mass-encryption early (sudden high-volume file modification on shares). Insecure (false) when no write-rate/rename anomaly alerting exists, so mass-encryption proceeds unobserved until shares are already encrypted.

config_backed_up_to_known_good.title: Config Backed Up to Known-Good
config_backed_up_to_known_good.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: whether the store's configuration/data is captured in a known-good backup that can be restored after compromise. Insecure (false) when no known-good baseline exists to recover from, compounding ransomware impact.

rollback_tested.title: Rollback / Restore Tested
rollback_tested.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: whether recovery/restore from backup is periodically tested so a real ransomware event can actually be reversed. Insecure (false) when restores are untested — backups may exist but fail when needed, leaving recovery impossible.

data_store_publicly_routable.title: File Store Publicly Routable
data_store_publicly_routable.description: Shared-vocabulary attestation: whether the file-storage host is reachable from a public/internet-routable interface. True means the NAS/file server is exposed to the open internet (insecure); the secure state is a store reachable only from trusted internal networks (false).

file_sharing_ports_internet_exposed.title: File-Sharing Ports Internet-Exposed
file_sharing_ports_internet_exposed.description: Whether the file-sharing service ports — SMB (TCP 445/139) and/or NFS (TCP/UDP 2049 + rpcbind 111) — are listening on a public interface or otherwise reachable from the internet. True is insecure; secure state firewalls 445/2049/111 to trusted client subnets only (false). Interpreted boolean — the assessor confirms reachability from an untrusted vantage rather than matching a raw port string.

segment_boundary_enforced.title: Segment Boundary Enforced
segment_boundary_enforced.description: Shared-vocabulary attestation: whether a network-segmentation boundary is enforced between the file-storage service and untrusted VLANs/segments, so file-sharing ports are not reachable from untrusted internal networks. The secure state is an enforced boundary (true); when no segmentation is enforced (false) the store is reachable from untrusted VLANs — the insecure condition this exposure fires on.

encrypted_at_rest.title: Volume Encrypted at Rest
encrypted_at_rest.description: Whether the underlying file-storage volume is encrypted at rest (BitLocker, LUKS/dm-crypt, or NAS volume encryption) with keys held in a KMS/HSM/TPM separate from the data. SMB3/NFS in-transit encryption does NOT satisfy this. True = volume encrypted at rest (secure); false = plaintext volume so stolen, lost, or decommissioned disks leak sensitive files (exposure). Shared workspace vocabulary.

media_sanitized_before_disposal.title: Media Sanitized Before Disposal
media_sanitized_before_disposal.description: Whether drives/volumes are sanitized per NIST SP 800-88r2 (Clear/Purge/Destroy at the level matched to data confidentiality impact) before reuse or disposal, with sanitization records or certificates of destruction retained. True = a sanitization process is in place and evidenced (secure); false = drives reused or disposed without sanitization, leaving recoverable data remanence (exposure).

secure_deletion_or_crypto_shred.title: Secure Deletion / Crypto-Shred
secure_deletion_or_crypto_shred.description: Whether retired media is rendered unrecoverable via cryptographic erase (destroying the at-rest encryption key so ciphertext is irrecoverable) or an equivalent Purge-level secure deletion. True = crypto-shred / secure-erase performed (secure); false = no secure-deletion mechanism, so residual data is recoverable from retired storage (exposure). Reinforces media_sanitized_before_disposal for the data-remanence facet. Shared workspace vocabulary.

access_audit_trail_enabled.title: File-Access Audit Trail Enabled
access_audit_trail_enabled.description: Whether object/file-access audit logging is enabled on sensitive shares (Windows SACL 'Audit Object Access' / Linux auditd file watches) and shipped to a central SIEM. When false, abnormal bulk reads of files go unrecorded so exfiltration is neither detected nor attributable. Shared workspace vocabulary.

dlp_egress_controls_enabled.title: DLP Egress Controls Enabled
dlp_egress_controls_enabled.description: Whether data-loss-prevention controls inspect and constrain sensitive files leaving the share (copy-off, sync, email) on egress paths. When false, sensitive files may be copied out at volume with no inspection or blocking, the compensating control for over-broad read access and insider/credential-theft exfiltration being absent. Shared workspace vocabulary.

bulk_export_monitored_and_alerted.title: Bulk Export Monitored and Alerted
bulk_export_monitored_and_alerted.description: Whether abnormal high-volume / bulk read-and-copy activity against the share is monitored and alerted (read-rate / bulk-export anomaly detection, e.g. SIEM analytics or UEBA on the audit stream). When false, a large-scale copy of files does not trigger any alert, so exfiltration proceeds silently even where individual access is technically logged. Shared workspace vocabulary.

unpatched_known_rce_cve.title: Known-Exploited RCE CVE Present
unpatched_known_rce_cve.description: Interpreted boolean: the NAS appliance OS or a bundled app runs a firmware/app version carrying a known-exploited (CISA KEV) remote-code-execution or improper-authorization CVE — e.g. QNAP HBS 3 CVE-2021-28799 (Qlocker) or Photo Station CVE-2022-27593 (DeadBolt). True when any outstanding KEV-listed exploitable CVE applies. Secure (hardened) value is false. Shared workspace vocabulary.

unnecessary_nas_apps_enabled.title: Unnecessary NAS Apps Enabled
unnecessary_nas_apps_enabled.description: Interpreted boolean: non-essential bundled NAS applications (e.g. Photo Station, Hybrid Backup Sync, media/web apps) are installed and enabled, expanding the appliance's exploitable attack surface beyond core file sharing. These bundled apps are the components most frequently carrying the mass-exploited KEV CVEs. Secure value is false; the exposure fires when true.

rate_limiting_or_lockout_enabled.title: Rate Limiting / Lockout Enabled
rate_limiting_or_lockout_enabled.description: Shared-vocabulary attestation: the store throttles failed authentication against its admin UIs and SMB/file shares via a server-side authentication rate limiter (SMB InvalidAuthenticationDelayTimeInMs non-zero, default 2000 ms on Windows Server 2025 / Windows 11 24H2) and/or account lockout, blunting high-rate online credential brute force. Secure value is true; the exposure fires when false (unthrottled brute force against exposed shares/admin).
